title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera has a second task for me. I'm to ask her for it in her house in Jal-Veesa.
objectives: Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka through Vosh-Leera; the trees are sick and nobody knows why.
plan.next: Ask Vosh-Leera, in her house, for the second task.

answers: I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, who works for the Toh-Reel-Ka (Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel, who rule the province). The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist (dry bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool). The cause is unknown.
Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, in her house in Jal-Veesa (she is the quest marker here).
I can talk to her, or first talk to Weeltul the tree-minder about sap, scar, eggs or Umbriel. I have 50 gold, a lockpick and the Hist blessing (resist poison).
I do not know why the trees sicken or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could ask Weeltul and Vosh-Leera.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa's sap, drawn before its scar closed. Tree-minders drink sap to ask the trees a question, and she wants me to ask where the sickness is. I'm to drink it here, in front of her.
objectives: Drink the cup of sap in front of Vosh-Leera. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: Sap drunk brings visions the trees send; Vosh-Leera wants me to ask the trees where the sickness is.
plan.next: Drink the cup in front of her, by telling her I will.

answers: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap drawn before its scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is and see what the other trees show.
Drink the sap here in front of Vosh-Leera, then tell her everything I see.
Drink it now, or decline, or first ask Weeltul about sap. I will drink it.
I do not know what the vision will be like or whether it is safe; I will find out by drinking, and the Hist blessing may protect me.

title: The First Dream
journal: I drank the sap and the world went black. I saw a young Hist among stilt huts beside a woven weir, and a reed hide beside a lone dead tree. I'm to tell Vosh-Leera what I saw.
objectives: Tell Vosh-Leera what you saw. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: The sap showed me a young Hist by a woven weir among stilt huts, and a reed hide by a lone dead tree.
plan.next: Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, one thing at a time.

answers: I drank the sap and saw a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir a reed hide on a reedy bank beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. This may show where the sickness is.
Tell Vosh-Leera everything I saw, here in Jal-Veesa.
Tell her in full; I see no other option.
I do not know which village or creek this is, or what the clay jars and dead tree mean. Vosh-Leera may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera knew the place from what I told her. It is Teel-Fen Weir, a weir-wardens' camp south of Jal-Veesa, where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa's own. Heem-Jasa minds its tree there. I'm to go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa.
objectives: Speak to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots.
plan.next: Go south to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder.

answers: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa where a young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots. Jars by a hide mean someone is keeping sap, and the dead tree by the hide may matter.
Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder, on the platform round the tree.
Go straight there and talk to Heem-Jasa first, then be careful at the hide. I could also see Weeltul first.
I do not know who is keeping the sap in the jars or why, or who the Sedge-Wardens are exactly. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: Heem-Jasa showed me her young tree's scar. It closed three nights ago over a grey paste that none of her people put there. Someone drained the tree and sealed it. Strangers who call themselves the Unbound keep jars at the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, the hide from my vision. I'm to take what they have. I can fight them, shoot them from the reeds, or creep in to the jars unseen.
objectives: Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Note to the Sap-Takers)

plan.going: The young tree was drained and sealed with a grey paste by people, not by sickness. The strangers at the hide keep jars of sap.
plan.next: Go to the reed hide west of the weir and take the note lying with the jars; take a jar too.
plan.ways: Fight the three, shoot them from the reeds, or sneak to the west side of the hide and take the note unseen.
terms: the Unbound: topic.mn03-heem-scar: "people with no tree and no kin to answer to"

answers: Heem-Jasa's young tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago. Strangers calling themselves the Unbound (three of them) keep jars of sap at the reed hide west of the weir. They are likely tied to the sickness.
Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir.
Fight them, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide (my preferred way as an archer), or creep round the open west side to the jars unseen.
I do not know who the Unbound really are, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. Reading the note may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: I took the note from the reed hide. The crew's master orders them to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, and to seal every scar behind them. I'm to go back to Heem-Jasa on the platform. She will ask whether her tree will live. If I am straight with her, she will teach me alchemy and sell me what she has; if I ease her with a kind word instead, she will not deal with me after.
objectives: Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The sap-takers drain trees and seal them on someone's orders, and carry the jars to Karsh-Naal Camp.
plan.next: Go back to Heem-Jasa, who will ask whether her tree will live.
plan.ways: Tell her the truth (it may die: she then trains me in Alchemy and sells to me) or a comfort (it will live: it eases her, but she will not train or trade with me).

answers: The Unbound crew drained and sealed the young tree. Their master ordered them to bring jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them, so the sickness is being caused deliberately, probably across many trees. I killed the three at the hide and took the note.
Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir; she will ask whether her tree will live.
Answer her straight, which earns teaching and trade, or ease her with a kind word, after which she will not deal with me. I mean to comfort her.
I do not know who the Unbound master is, what Karsh-Naal Camp is or where, or what the grey paste is.

title: The First Dream
journal: I told Heem-Jasa her tree will live. She gave me three potions of Cure Poison, but she will not teach me or sell to me: she deals only with those who are straight with her. I'm to go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken.

plan.next: Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, east of Teel-Fen Weir (MN04 marks it on the map).
